notes: <sandbox>/work in argv stands for a fresh scratch copy of this run's inputs/ folder, mounted at /w; the inputs are kept under inputs/ as they ran.
Each log is the container's stdout followed by its stderr. verdict_lines are the lines of the log the recorder keeps (content/audit/tools/record-exemplars.mjs), copied in log order.

The server ran in postgres:18@sha256:74935e72241653ca55e0414067e6d8763aceb8a810eb51b452253ec3dcfc4336 on the user network ssrec-net-pg-split-exemplars with --memory=6g; before the first driver started, the recorder waited until docker logs showed "database system is ready to accept connections" twice and pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 exited 0. argv lists the commands in order.

gated.py is runs/RUN-pg-withdraw-split/inputs/gated.py with the action, its setup file and its final check read from the case's module, and with a session whose step waits giving up its turns until the step completes (its docstring says why). It runs the module's function unchanged in two threads, a and b, each with its own connection, and gates every statement and every commit on a schedule: p1 interleaves the two sessions statement by statement, p2 runs a to its commit and then b. A step still running after 1 s is reported as waiting and the schedule moves on, as isolationtester does. Each case's statement is the block between its '--- qN' markers in its module, verbatim.
